developers.developersAppearHint: Developers will appear here after they register via invite

permissions.pageSubtitle: Manage identity, eligibility, role defaults, individual access, and restrictions
permissions.overviewLoadFailed: Could not load the overview data.
permissions.overviewContextAllMapped: Every contextual role maps to a profile
permissions.overviewScopeHint: Predicates implemented — verification only, not enforced
permissions.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, email, or CID...
permissions.individualAccessHint: Use Individual Access only when a specific person needs permissions different from their normal role and default profile.
permissions.accessSetupHint: Access Setup defines normal access in two steps. Access Profiles: create the reusable permission packages. Role Defaults: connect each role to the profile it receives automatically.
permissions.noDefaultsHint: Use the Set Role Default Profile button to assign a default profile
permissions.defaultAccessHint: Role Defaults = the capabilities automatically given to everyone with this role (via their default Access Profile).
permissions.defaultAccessHintTail: Individual overrides and grants are managed in the Individual Access tab.
permissions.roleDefaultsMatrixHint: ✓ = default profile for this role · — = none set. Click a cell to assign or change the default.
permissions.roleDefaultsCellSet: Click to set as default profile for {role}
permissions.profileInUseWarning: This profile is currently assigned as the default access profile for {roles}. Changes will affect users who inherit this profile.
permissions.eligibilityMatrixHint: E = eligible · D = explicitly denied · — = unset (fail-closed). Click a cell to edit that identity.
permissions.eligibilityNoPermission: You do not have permission to modify eligibility (permissions.configure_eligibility is required)
permissions.eligibilityReadOnly: Read-only — you do not hold the permissions.configure_eligibility capability
permissions.eligibilityHint: Eligibility defines who MAY receive a feature. It does not grant access — capabilities (Default Access profiles / Individual Access grants) decide what the person can actually do.
permissions.eligibilityLegend: Eligible = may receive the feature. Not eligible = explicitly denied (deny wins). Unset = no row (missing rows fail closed to deny). Changes apply immediately to the authorization resolver.
permissions.profilesIntro: Access Profiles define what capabilities a user gets. Each role has a default profile; users can be assigned a specific profile to override the role default.
permissions.assignHint: This overrides the user's role default profile. Set profile to empty to remove the override.
permissions.selectProfileRemoveOverride: -- Select profile (leave empty to remove override) --
permissions.roleDefaultHint: Choose which access profile a role uses by default. All users with that role (who don't have an individual override) will use this profile.
permissions.selectProfilePrompt: Choose a profile from the list to view and edit its permissions.
permissions.profileChangeAffectsUsers: Changes will affect every user who inherits this profile.
permissions.profileEligibilityFilterHint: Showing only features that the role(s) using this profile are eligible for: {roles}
permissions.profileNoRolesHint: This profile is not the default profile of any role — all features are shown.
permissions.profileNoEligibleFeatures: None of this profile's roles are eligible for any feature — nothing to show.
permissions.viewBaseHint: View is the base capability: granting edit/create/delete auto-grants View, and View can't be removed while other capabilities are enabled.
permissions.subsectionLevelHint: One access level per feature — its subsections are protected by the same modules, so choosing a level here applies to the whole feature.
permissions.viewRequiredMsg: View is required — disable the other capabilities before removing it.
permissions.responsibilitiesIntro: Responsibilities define operational ownership — what dashboards, navigation, and reports a user sees. They are NOT permissions.
permissions.responsibilitiesSearchPlaceholder: Search user by name, email, or CID...
permissions.responsibilityAccessIntro: Choose which roles can actually use the feature each responsibility grants. The warnings across the app read this configuration and it applies immediately.
permissions.auditSearch: Search actor, target, action, module, capability or details…
permissions.governanceIntro: Operational overview of membership and permission activity. Informational only — no automatic changes are made from here.
permissions.whyMembershipNotContributing: Expired membership does not contribute to access
permissions.whyAccountIntact: Membership expiration never deletes the account — it only stops group-derived access.
permissions.contextRolesHint: Maps each contextual role (what someone is inside a Program / Venture / Learning / Investor context) to the access profile that should seed their capabilities. Governance registry only in this phase — the resolver does not read it yet, so nothing here changes effective access. Scope arrives in Phase 5.
permissions.contextRolesLoadFailed: Could not load the context-role registry.
permissions.contextRolesReasonPlaceholder: Reason for these changes (optional — recorded in the audit log)
permissions.contextRolesHolderHint: Holder counts are informational — how many relationships of this kind exist today.
permissions.scopePoliciesIntro: Record-level scope policies are enforced at the data layer by the Scope Engine (roadmap Phase 5). This registry is the governance surface for those policies — nothing here authorizes anything yet.
permissions.scopePoliciesStatus: Engine core implemented — verification only, not enforced (Phase 5)
permissions.scopePoliciesImplemented: Predicate implemented — verification only (not enforced on routes yet)
permissions.scopePoliciesRowVentureBody: Founder and team capabilities apply only to ventures the person belongs to.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowProgramBody: Program-staff and participant capabilities apply per program membership and assignment.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowLearningBody: Learner capabilities apply to the learner's own enrollments.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowTeamBody: Team-entity access is limited to the team's own records.
permissions.reasonPlaceholder: Why is this change being made? (optional — recorded in the audit log)
permissions.reasonLabel: Reason recorded in the permission audit log
permissions.defaultsMatrixHint: What each identity receives by default — rows expand Feature → Module. Module access is derived from capabilities; modules with zero capabilities stay visible. Editing opens a drawer; changes go to the pending tray for review before saving.
permissions.matrixLoadFailed: Could not load the permission matrix.
permissions.matrixNoDefaultProfileHint: This identity has no default access profile yet — set one in Access Profiles / Role Defaults before editing capabilities here.
permissions.matrixNoPendingChanges: No pending changes for this module.
permissions.userMatrixHint: Why can this user do what they do? Pick a user to see every capability decomposed into its sources — Profile | Group | Grant | Restriction — with the Effective result. Scope is a separate column (engine arrives in a later phase).
permissions.userMatrixEmpty: No capabilities found for this user.
permissions.userMatrixFootnote: Sources: profile (base), groups, individual grants; restrictions remove the capability entirely (they beat grants). Effective = any source minus restrictions. Scope displays as All until the scope engine (P4) ships — the server remains authoritative.
permissions.catalogHint: Read-only registry of every Feature → Module → Capability the enforcement layer understands. Locked modules (Super Admin-only decisions) and retired capabilities are marked, never hidden.
permissions.catalogNoModules: No modules mapped to this feature yet.
permissions.scopePoliciesHint: Planned for a later phase (P4): which data each capability may operate on (assigned ventures, own venture…).
permissions.groupsHint: Group capability editing lives in the governance screens; protected-organization rules are enforced by org_membership.
permissions.enforcementNoteHint: This center manages configuration and visibility. Authorization is enforced server-side on every API; hiding a menu is never authorization.
